title: Affirmative defenses
summary: An affirmative defense supplies an additional reason the defendant should avoid or limit liability even when the claim’s ordinary allegations are assumed. It performs a different role from a denial.
notes: Not every unpleaded defense is inevitably lost. Amendment, notice, consent, and prejudice may matter under the governing rule and cases.

sections.Meaning: An affirmative defense supplies an additional reason the defendant should avoid or limit liability even when the claim’s ordinary allegations are assumed. It performs a different role from a denial.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the defense, the rule requiring notice, when it was raised, and whether omission deprived the other side of a fair opportunity to litigate. Ingraham examines a damages limitation raised only after trial.
